title: Differentiation: Limits and Rules
seo_title: Differentiation – SSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find limits; differentiate from first principles; differentiate polynomials and simple functions using the power rule and the chain rule. (summary of the NERDC SSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 maths worksheets on introductory calculus: limits, first principles, the power rule, derivatives at a point and the chain rule. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Multiply by the power, then take 1 from it.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • dy/dx is the gradient of the curve at any point.
  • d/dx(axⁿ) = naxⁿ⁻¹; the derivative of a constant is 0.
  • To find the gradient at a point, put its x-value into dy/dx.

Examples

Example

y = 3x² − 5x + 2

6x − 5

Answer: dy/dx = 6x − 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not taking 1 from the powerx³ → 3x².
Keeping the constantA constant differentiates to 0.
Putting x into y instead of dy/dxGradient uses dy/dx.

items.q: Using the first principle, f(x) = 3x² − x + 2. What is limh→0 [f(x + h) − f(x)] ÷ h?
